label: copy-phase input f fed back early in the copy (f was one of the first three original tokens)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the fed-back input is the letter f (43670 of 43672 dev activations have in_tok = f). It never fires on f during the original phase or at the delimiter. It is strongest on early copy steps: recall_idx 1-3, meaning f was original token 0, 1 or 2, account for about 98% of activation mass. Top activations (about 3.3-3.5) come from f at the first copy-input step, right after the model outputs f as original token 0, or at position 1. It is weak or absent when f is fed back later in the copy (recall_idx >= 4) and on the final output step. In the quartile examples, magnitude tends to be lower when f appears later in the sequence (e.g. 2 r f ... gives 0.07 relative to max). Missed activations are negligible (2 steps, <0.1% of mass). Remaining false positives are mostly f inputs at recall_idx 3 in short sequences, or weak cases.

issues: The core claims hold. The feature is exclusive to the copy phase (original and delimiter phases are 0 active). It is essentially exclusive to in_tok f: 43670 of 43672 dev activations. It never fires on the first occurrence of a token (in_first=1 is 0 active). recall_idx 1-2 hold 84% of mass and recall_idx 3 holds 13.5%. recall_idx >= 4 has test precision 0.097 and 2.3% of mass. The top activations are f fed back at copy steps 1-2, around 3.2-3.5.

Systematic gap: the predicate keeps to_go == 1 (f fed back at the second-to-last output step), but that class is mostly inactive. It has test precision 0.255 and only 0.8% of mass, and it makes up about half of the predicate's 6929 test false positives (mostly short sequences, L = 4-5, e.g. 'f b m z <DEL> *f* b m'). The explanation says the feature is only weak on the final step, but it is just as weak one step earlier.

Using to_go >= 2 instead of to_go >= 1 raises test F1 from 0.879 to 0.902 (precision 0.851 to 0.930, recall 0.908 to 0.876, mass recall 0.977 to 0.969). This is the same as requiring L - recall_idx >= 3. to_go >= 3 overshoots (F1 0.837).

The misses left under the to_go >= 2 predicate are very weak activations (about 0.04-0.13 of max): late f inputs (recall_idx >= 4) and f near the end of short sequences. This is scattered low-mass noise (3.1% of mass), not a strong class.

The label is fine but loose: activation depends on both being early in the copy (recall_idx <= 3) and having at least 2 outputs still to come. In short sequences (L = 3-5) it rarely fires even at early recall_idx.
